text_blocks.snippet: Type 1 diabetes is a chronic autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. This leads to the body being unable to produce insulin, a hormone that regulates blood sugar levels. Without sufficient insulin, glucose (sugar) cannot be effectively transported from the blood into cells for energy, resulting in high blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: a chronic autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas

list.title: Insulin Deficiency:
list.snippet: The pancreas, specifically the beta cells within the islets of Langerhans, are destroyed, leading to little to no insulin production.

list.title: High Blood Sugar:
list.snippet: Without sufficient insulin, glucose accumulates in the bloodstream, leading to hyperglycemia (high blood sugar).
